title: Kerala’s Kumbh Mela faces fresh uncertainty as organisers split over leadership, finances
content: Malappuram: The attempt to revive the historic Mahamagha Mahotsavam at Thirunnavaya as Kerala's own 'Kumbh Mela' is facing a fresh organisational crisis, with competing groups staking claims over the festival's future, allegations of financial irregularities from its January 2026 edition and disagreements over leadership threatening to cloud preparations for the next event. The festival, held on the banks of the Bharathapuzha at Thirunavaya in Malappuram district in January 2026 after a gap of more than 230 years, drew lakhs of devotees and attracted national political attention, especially due to the boycotting of Congress and left parties. The festival's revival marked a significant moment in religious mobilisation in Kerala, bringing together various Hindu spiritual organisations, sannyasi communities and Sangh Parivar organisations. However, differences within its organising network have now overshadowed the event's success, leaving the management of the next edition uncertain as preparations for 2027 begin. At the centre of the dispute is the absence of Anandavanam Bharati, a Mahamandaleshwar of the Juna Akhada who played a prominent role in reviving and organising the 2026 festival, from recent discussions about the next edition. A statement issued on Friday by the Margadarshaka Mandalam, a collective of Hindu spiritual leaders, has brought the disagreements into sharper focus by detailing disputes over organisational authority, the recognition of long-standing organisers and allegations concerning the handling of festival revenue. The Margadarshaka Mandalam, led by Swami Chidananda Puri and general secretary Swami Satswaroopananda Saraswati, is pursuing efforts to organise the next festival with the participation of the local committees from both banks of the river. Meanwhile, Anandavanam Bharati is expected to convene another meeting of his supporters and associates in the first week of November. The competing initiatives have raised questions about whether the groups can reach an understanding or whether preparations will proceed along separate tracks. Dispute over leadership and financial accountability According to the Margadarshaka Mandalam's statement, several disputes emerged within the committee associated with the 2026 festival after Anandavanam Bharati joined its activities. The statement says disagreements intensified over what the organisers regarded as inadequate recognition of the committees that had conducted the festival for several consecutive years, publicity portraying the event as having begun only in 2025 under the leadership of the Juna Akhada, and an announcement that the next festival would be held over 51 days, allegedly made without consultation. The most serious allegations concern the festival's finances. The Margadarshaka Mandalam claims that Anandavanam Bharati and those associated with him took control of a substantial portion of the revenue generated during the event without the knowledge or consent of the organising committee, while leaving the committee to bear the expenses and liabilities. Meanwhile, Anandavanam Bharati told Onmanorama that he will respond to the accusations and explain his plans for the festival after Vijayadashami. The statement issued by the Margadarshaka Mandalam says the disagreements reached a point where the organisers were unable even to constitute an organising committee for the next edition, and its leaders, including Swami Chidananda Puri, held discussions with Anandavanam Bharati and representatives of Hindu organisations, proposing that the festival be organised collectively, with the involvement of spiritual leaders and institutions from across Kerala. According to the statement, Anandavanam Bharati rejected the proposal, maintaining that he would organise the Kerala Kumbh Mela under the leadership of the Juna Akhada, irrespective of whether the other groups participated...
